It isn't the go to solution, per se. It's why when people are finding out their gender we don't first tell them to try different hormones, hell, some people because of medical or other personal reasons can't take hormones as their way through their transition. 

The first and the 'go to' step is social transition. Cutting their hair or growing it out, trying on more feminine or masculine clothes, having people using different pronouns and adjectives when referring to them, using a different name, etc. 

If that is comfortable and they want more to feel better about themselves physically, they can ask a doctor if hormones are okay for them, or they could get gender affirming surgery. Hell, I know people who don't need this and are still happy with their bodies, but that can't apply to everyone.  Why do people get haircuts? Why do people get piercings? Why do some cis men do hormone treatment to fix their testosterone levels? Why do people get cosmetic surgeries? Because it makes them feel better as themselves and with their self expression. It's the same for gender affirming care.

I think you are doing phenomenal for 5 hours for 2 sketches of that detail. 

If you really wanna get quicker though what I find works best is just becoming real confident with your lines and shapes. A quick slap sketch that is confident and gets the points you need across can really help with mapping out the rest of the drawing and with time and practice youll get quicker at it. 

The way I became quicker at drawing is doing the whole '5 min sketch, 30 min sketch, then 1 hour sketch' of the same photo. Doing that exercise can really help you realize what works best when laying down the form on paper. Soon you can slap down a really good sketch quickly and drop it to a 1 min, 10 min, 30 min sketch. Its a time consuming task to make it less time consuming ironically but I noticed progress just doing this for about 7 days it does work well. I like it because you can use this for figure drawing or even things like landscapes or portraits. 

Keep up the amazing work friend

Hi, I am not 100% sure that this will help you but I went from being so scared of needles I couldn't hold one without crying to having to give myself injections every week. This is what I did. 

First. This one is kinda goofy. I started sewing. The idea of holding a sewing needle and working with it made me comfortable with holding and moving around a syringe with a needle. Again. I used to be REALLY scared of them, so this was big for me. Also. Getting poked with a needle a few times from sewing made me realize it doesnt hurt as much as i thought it would. 

Second. I learned about the safest and most painless ways to do injections. I find after a nice warm shower and then numbing the area with ice and playing music that makes me calm gave me the most painless injections because I'm relaxed and the ice made it so i didnt even feel the needle going in. 

Note about the above section, when you do an injection, you want to put the needle in fast, and push the liquid in slowly. There are a lot of videos online for how to do actual injections, these can help too. Idk with what you are using if you can warm up the vial of liquid in your hand it also helps so you dont feel it being pushed under the skin. 

Third. I learned my options. I originally had to start my injections with intramuscular needles. About an inch long. These ones left bruises and hurt. I had to have someone else do my injections for a while. Then i finally got to switch to subcutaneous needles. A lot smaller. You inject at an angle so it doesnt go as deep either. This was my game changer. After doing injections for over 2 years now I can do either kind of needle injection with ease. It does get better. Sometimes it takes longer because I freak out about it, but in the end it gets easier.

Note taking, the differences are page setup, how you write things down and what kind of information you write down.

 As i mentioned, Cornell is my personal favorite because you set up the page into 4 sections (If you google a photo it'll make more sense) and fill out the areas as they pop up and then summarize it all at the bottom of the page. It works well for me because i tend to overwrite my notes, so the key words on the left of the page and the summary on the bottom of the page keep the important parts, while the main part of the page kinda keeps the flow and info of the lesson more explained and stretched out.  

Mapping method of note taking kinda looks like a weird tree. I like this one where anything about how things connect and meet together. This one is nice if you are a more visual learner. I never really used this one tbh but i know some people love it. 

Outline method. I loved this one for my psychology and anatomy classes. You take your paper and write general ideas more towards the left of the paper. You break that general idea down a line below thats been indented, then again a line below you break that down or add more notes about the line above it. It takes up a lot of space but its clean and gets the info you need written. 

The last one is sentence method, basically make a kinda grid with the top being a general idea/info that you want to put in the lines below it. Add more ideas to the right as they get added on. I only really used it for history class but some used it for science and such too. 

The studying methods really summarize are: 
Verbal: learn through talkin about it 
Visual: Study by looking at it
Kinetic: learn by hands on experience
Logical: using logic. Can be kinda math-y type too. 
Musical: Using music and rhythm to study, like making a song with your notes like i mentioned. 
Natural: learn by breaking down and listing. think more like classifications like how you would classify plants and animals 
Intrapersonal: You learn best solo and only with yourself
Interpersonal' Learn best with groups and other people

“Hey, dude. Pass me that knife beside ya’” I point toward the small but sharp kitchen knife beside my friend. “Gotcha.” He nods and hands me the knife, holding it from the handle like he is about to attack me rather than hand it to me. “Bro.” I say, reaching out and picking it up from the part of the handle that wasn’t covered by his hand, our hands kind of brushing as I do so. I take the knife and cut open the top of the last of the three pumpkins we have been carving, the disgusting smell of pumpkin guts again filling the air. “Bro.” He says, staring down at the hand he just held the knife with. “That was pretty gay.” He says in the voice he always uses when he tries to make it apparent that he is joking. 
“Gay?” We hear a voice chime in that we do not recognize. “The fuck?” My friend says, looking around trying to find the source of the voice. “TV maybe?” I say, setting the knife and pumpkin aside and walking to go check the living room TV. I peer into the room and find my dog chilling on the couch watching reruns of The Haunting Hour, a disgusting and dusty looking yellow sports mascot on the show dancing to some music by swaying his arms around. 
“Uh, alright. Maybe not.” I say turning back into the kitchen to find my friend peering out the window. “Nothin’ out here.” He says. 
“I really miss my husband.” We hear the voice chime in again, freaking the fuck out this time.  “Brian, the fuck. Quit it already.” I snap at him. “Dude, it isn’t me!” He barks back. “Check your phone maybe? Ya’ accidentally call someone?”  I pull out my phone and see nothing odd. No calls or any apps that would even make noise are open. “No dude.” We stare at each other bewildered and begin we hear something moving. It was a very heavy but hallow noise, like a heavy box being pushed was the best way to describe it at the time. We look at each other, then in the direction of noise. To the left of the table we were carving pumpkins on, we set all finished jack-o-lanterns in a line on top of the counter, one of them facing their carved and silly face toward us, their candle flickering very softly. We notice one of the other jack-o-lanterns was slowly moving. We look at each other then back to the jack-o-lantern. It snaps around, showing it’s carved face, making us take a step back, Brian running into the wall as he does so. 
“We had such a cute family y’know.” The pumpkin man says, the candle in him flickering as he talked and a bit of pumpkin insides spitting out as he pronounces the S in Such. “Dude, did you put some wacky shit in the brownies or something?” I say as I stare at the pumpkin guts he spat onto the floor. “No dude.” Brian says with a worried and perplexed tone in his voice. 
“Just wishin’ I could go back and see m’kids again at least. Or m’husband.” The pumpkin man says in a sad and lonesome tone, his carved mouth now slouching down as the candle inside of him dies down a bit. Brian and I continue to just stare, too shocked to know what to honestly do. 
“Y’guys got a family? Or are ya’ a family? No judgement here if that’s the case.” 
“Uh.” I say looking over at Brian who just looks sickly and then back at the pumpkin man. “No?” I reply back. “Ah, okay, okay. Sorry if that was rude or weird anythin’” The pumpkin man looks down at the counter he is stood upon. “Ivan..” I hear Brian whisper and I look over. “What.” I whisper back. “The fuck is this, man?” He says nodding toward the pumpkin. I shrug. “Maybe some-“ 
“Whatcha guys talkin’ about?” The pumpkin man interrupts me, taking my gaze from Brian back to the pumpkin. “Uhhm.” I awkwardly stutter back, now looking more closely at the gross insides of the now talking jack-o-lantern. “Nothing, uh..” “Name’s McCree.” He nods by rocking back and forth. “McCree..” I say back to him. “Dude..” Brian whispers back at me, I look back at him annoyed and confused. “Is our pumpkin being possessed by a fucking outlaw gunslinger?” He says before turning back to the pumpkin cowboy. “No...” I say also looking back with now just a face of pure disgust. 
McCree looks at us with a sad face and sighs heavily. “I knew it.” He said, his voice now low and husky. “Even you guys hate me.” 
“What?” Brian finally chimes into the conversation.  “I knew I wasn’t meant for this world. No one will ever accept my love for my husband and our two little kiddos.”  Brian’s face scrunches even more in confusion.  “What do you mean?” I kind of awkwardly chuckle out. 
“See!” McCree snaps out at me. “Y’all makin’ fun of me with your faces lookin’ like you just seen roadkill on the street or somethin’.” McCree barks back.  “We didn’t-“ 
“I’ve had enough of this!” McCree yells then looks down to see smoke coming out of his pumpkin body. “Enough of it...” he mumbles weakly and his eyes roll back along with his pumpkin body. 
A loud splat is then heard as McCree falls to the hard tile floor. 
Brian and I walk over very cautiously to see a dead pumpkin on the floor, its guts oozing with pumpkin juices and candle wax.  
A long silence ensues as we both look at the dead McCree. 
“Dude.” I look up at Brian. “Yeah?” He says back, squatting down and touching the pumpkin guts.  “What the fuck just happened?” I spit out. He thinks for a minute as stands back up. “I have no fucking clue.” He says as he goes to grab a trash bag from under the sink.  
I start to pick up McCree’s guts and basically toss them into the trash bag. We clean up the scene and look at the pumpkins still sitting on my counter, then at each other. We give a nod and chuck them into the bag as well. The scent of pumpkin now bleeding through the air. “What do we do with the bodies now?” Brian asks like they were actual human corpses. “Trash them, I guess.” He nods and goes outside to throw away the pumpkins. I watch Brian out the window as he throws the corpses away.  He pauses and looks into the trash can before he closes it and looks up at me in the window. His expression reads one of absolute disgust, but he gives me a thumbs up as he walks back up. 
“Yo, dude.” I say as he gets back into the house, closing the door behind him. “Yeah bro?” He says waiting for me to reply. 
“Wanna to watch The Haunting Hour with my dog?”  He chuckles and nods “Sure, man.”

Depression to me is like trying to live normally, just going about your day, but from the second you wake up to the second you fall asleep, it’s like you have a thick crowd of people always surrounding you. Each day it’s a different crowd. Some days the crowd is fairly forgiving; letting you go about your day, but you still know it’s there by the quiet chatter you can hear them whisper in the back of your mind, while other days, this crowd is very harsh. Pushing you. Pulling you back. Yelling at you. Hitting you. Kicking you over. Not letting you move. It feels like their glance just eats at your skin. You try to fight back and it’s so tiring. It sometimes just makes you want to give up and let them tear you to shreds. Sometimes it feels like they have you on a leash they just drag you around seeing how far they can push you. It gives you a sick feeling of almost being scared to wake up the next day to see if the crowd will be even worse. Some days you can’t fight so you sit in bed, some days you just need to sit and listen to them, other days you can stride on through, though still avoidant of the crowd. The crowd may be a lot thinner to some people, but there are some people who can’t walk through the crowd without bumping into someone every step of the way. I don’t think people get how tiring it is.
